claims: NASA launched the Artemis II mission on Wednesday, April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT (22:35 UTC).
The Artemis II mission is a 10-day crewed test flight around the Moon.
The Artemis II mission lifted off from Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
The Artemis II mission is the first human mission to the lunar vicinity in over 50 years.
The launch vehicle for Artemis II is the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
The spacecraft for Artemis II is the Orion capsule.
The Artemis II crew consists of Reid Wiseman (Commander), Victor Glover (Pilot), Christina Koch (Mission Specialist), and Jeremy Hansen (CSA - Mission Specialist).
The mission goal of Artemis II is to test the human-rated systems in deep space to prepare for future lunar landings.
The Artemis II mission achieved insertion into Earth's orbit.
The Artemis II mission is proceeding toward a crewed flyby around the Moon.
The Artemis II mission will return to Earth.
